commits.message:
fix(pretty): a container's compact try is charged for the key it sits under (rich-pretty-xms)

Pretty's fit-on-one-line decision for a nested container budgeted the
remaining width as maxWidth minus the indent alone, which is only the true
remaining width when nothing precedes the value on its line. A value under
a key — `metadata: { ... }` — has that key's width and separator eaten
from the same line, uncounted, so a container could pass the fit test and
still overrun the width once its key was prepended, wrapping mid-container.

Frame now carries `column`: where a value's text actually begins on the
line it lands on, threaded through `_expandSlot` per hole (so a Map
entry's `" => "` and a second hole are charged too, and a multi-line
insert resets the column to its own last line rather than accumulating
across lines that were never on the same row). The one-line probe path
already tracked this correctly via its shrinking `budget`; only the
lay-out path's own compact try was deriving the budget from depth instead
of position.

fix(docs): drop double-stacked newlines in group.md's Group examples (rich-flexstrip-5kf.c4u) (#147)

commit f1fa4c67 (rich-text-5ai) made RichText.render() draw its `end`
unconditionally. All three Group examples on docs/group.md built their
RichText/renderMarkup content with a literal trailing "\n" in the text
AND relied on the default end ("\n"), so every item printed a spurious
blank line after it. Drop the literal "\n"s and let the default `end`
supply the line break, matching what the page's shown output already
claims. Also corrects the explanatory paragraph, which asserted
`console.print` (not RichText itself) draws the default `end` -- true
before f1fa4c67, false since.
